newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay stocks end lower after early rally fizzles.
newsitem.headline: Bombay stocks end lower after early rally fizzles.

text.p: Bombay shares closed slightly lower on Wednesday in a session dominated by speculative action, dealers said.
Traders said the slide near the session's close took them by surprise, but attributed the fall to no single major factor.
"There was no reason for the market to have dropped as it did today," said chief dealer Sanjeev Choithani at brokers Pashupati Advani. "This is a big speculative game going on."
The Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) 30-share index fell 74.33 points from the day's high of 3,426.67 to end at 3,352.34 -- a net loss of 25.29 points or 0.75 percent over Tuesday's close.
"It's very difficult to understand the market trend. There's hardly any institutional activity," said a dealer at a local brokerage.
Positive remarks by Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda helped rally share prices in morning trade.
The Economic Times newspaper said on Wednesday that Deve Gowda had hinted the 1997 budget, due at the end of February, would include a package of measures to boost investor sentiment.
"When we present the budget, there will be more indications for investors to get a further favourable investment message," the paper quoted Gowda as telling a news conference.

India's fourth largest cement firm, Gujarat Ambuja Cements, said on Wednesday its net profit for the first half ending December 1996, rose 19.5 percent to 489.8 million rupees against 409.70 million in the corresponding period a year ago.
The share lost 6.75 rupees or 2.72 percent to 241.25 in volumes of 629,648 shares.
SBI was down 7.0 rupees to 261.50 rupees, Reliance 5.50 to 261.0, TISCO 4.0 to 181.50, ITC 7.25 to 378.25 and ACC 30.0 to 1,249.0.
